topic: Generalize the staffing trade-offs and dependencies matrix (remove the firm focus) into an interactive tool that lets a recruiter at a small technical company narrow the trade-offs for a particular job opening or requisition, with an interactive dependency graph of the narrowed field, mitigations, and links to technical solutions or enablers. Then generalize further, base it in best practices, reference all information, and make it as detailed and robust as FAR Out. The original 60 trade-offs and their eight categories are best guesses; more rigor is needed for both.
question: For a small technical firm whose hires must satisfy a contract or a customer, what actually constrains filling and keeping a position at each stage from workforce planning to handover; what does the evidence say each lever does and does not do; which regulatory and contractual gates bind a given opening; how do the constraints depend on one another; and what public data, programs and tools can a recruiter without an HR department put to work?

in: customer-governed small firms: federal prime and subcontractors, cleared and uncleared, and any small technical firm whose hires must satisfy a labor category, a key-personnel clause, a rate ceiling, a clearance or a customer approval
the four literatures: personnel selection (I/O psychology), turnover and retention, the labor economics of hiring and training, and the contractor-specific regulatory gates
the lifecycle stages the selection and turnover literatures use: plan, attract, select, offer, clear and start, onboard, develop, retain, hand over

the gates: E-Verify and I-9, clearance sponsorship and Trusted Workforce 2.0, export control (ITAR/EAR U.S. persons), VEVRAA and Section 503 plans, EEO and the Uniform Guidelines, background checks and the Fair Chance Act, drug-free workforce, Service Contract Act wage determinations, key-personnel and labor-category approval, compensation allowability (FAR 31.205-6), state pay-transparency, salary-history, non-compete and AI-hiring laws

public benchmarks and indicators with their dates: BLS JOLTS and OEWS, employee tenure, SHRM time-to-fill and cost-per-hire, DCSA/TW 2.0 timeliness and inventory, ClearanceJobs compensation, ODNI clearance population

programs and enablers: DoD SkillBridge, Hiring Our Heroes, registered apprenticeship, Handshake, O*NET, NICE framework, GSA CALC+, tooling categories (ATS, talent CRM, scheduling, assessment, dashboards), recorded as stated

what changed in 2025-26: EO 14173 and OFCCP's three final rules, the FTC non-compete rule's end, the H-1B fee proclamation and rulemaking, state law effective dates, SkillBridge employer mandates, TW 2.0 milestones, GAO findings on clearance data
out: state and local government contracting as a customer model (federal and prime customers only)
federal civil-service hiring (Title 5, USAJOBS) except where a contractor competes with it for the same people
staffing agencies and recruiting firms as a business; fee structures appear only as facts in enabler records
immigration law beyond what an employer must know to sponsor or hire (the H-1B fee and E-Verify are in; visa strategy is out)
benefits design, payroll administration and HR information systems beyond their role in a lever
anything tailored to a specific firm; no firm is named anywhere in the pack or the app
recommendations of paid consultants, tools or memberships; fees are reported as facts with sources

interview.q: Generalize the staffing matrix, remove the firm focus, and make an interactive tool for a recruiter at a small tech company?
interview.answer: Yes; a tool that narrows the trade-offs for a particular job opening or requisition, with an interactive dependency graph of the narrowed field, mitigations, and links to technical solutions or enablers.

Generalize more, base it in best practices, reference all information; as detailed and robust as FAR Out. The original 60 trade-offs are just best guesses; we need more rigor. That applies to their categories as well.

The Alabama Mental Health Explorer systems map: the graph gives information about each node, the edges carry information about the dependencies, and the dependencies are listed below the node information panel.

interview.q: Which boundary? (three cuts offered from the field sketch)
interview.answer: Customer-governed small firms: federal primes and subs, cleared and uncleared; all four literatures plus the contractor gates. Out: state and local contracting, civil-service hiring, staffing agencies as a business.

interview.q: What organises the records, replacing the A-H categories?
interview.answer: Lifecycle stages: plan, attract, select, offer, clear and start, onboard, develop, retain, hand over; gates and levers cross-cut; the pathfinder starts from the observed failure point.
Evidence-graded practice guide: every lever carries an evidence grade and a controversies section covers cognitive-ability validity, turnover cost, skills-based hiring and pay transparency.
Key Personnel; settings as FAR Out: public GitHub Pages, no firm named, no Zotero, no self-check questions.

evidence_grades.meta-analysis: a published meta-analysis or systematic review; the effect size is quoted with its k and N as reported
evidence_grades.field-experiment: a randomized or natural experiment in real hiring or employment settings
evidence_grades.quasi-experimental: difference-in-differences, regression discontinuity or matched designs on administrative or firm data
evidence_grades.observational: cross-sectional or longitudinal survey research without a causal design
evidence_grades.practitioner-survey: SHRM, ClearanceJobs, Gallup and similar; benchmark facts only, publisher and year named
evidence_grades.regulation: statute, CFR, FAR/DFARS, executive order, agency directive; binds regardless of evidence
evidence_grades.guidance: an agency's or standards body's recommended practice (OPM, EEOC, ISO 30414); not binding, cited as guidance
evidence_grades.synthesis: a conclusion no cited work states on its own; marked visibly in the app and listed on /methods

corpus_profile.concentration: Selection validity rests on one 2022 meta-analysis and the 1998 estimate it revised; retention on one 2018 meta-analysis; the clearance figures on one official report series and a vendor's restatement of DCSA presentations; the state overlay on about fourteen compilations, each a law-firm, vendor or advocacy page, with only three statutes read outside Alabama; the Alabama row and its six state gates rest on the Code of Alabama, enrolled acts and agency pages (sweep 9), eight of those sections read on a mirror of the Code pending the official viewer. Several effect sizes come from single-firm studies (Shaw and Lazear; Allen 2006; Speer et al.; Card et al.) and are carried with their population named. About a third of the 312 references are governing texts or official guidance carried as background.
corpus_profile.dissent_note: the six controversy records carry each side with its citation (cognitive-ability validity; skills-based hiring; pay transparency; the clearance timeliness figures; who pays for training; the cost of turnover)
